claims.text: The Jardin des Tuileries was first created as a public garden in 1564.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It was directly named after the old tile factories, or 'tuileries', that previously occupied this large site.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The impressive gardens were famously designed by the renowned landscape architect André Le Nôtre.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: They were originally built adjoining the grand royal Tuileries Palace, which has sadly since been lost.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Lying immediately west of the Louvre, these semi-formal gardens now act as a beautiful outdoor gallery for modern sculpture.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, this vast public park also permanently encloses the popular Musée de l'Orangerie and the Jeu de Paume.
claims.subject: self
